solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slow movement is this, bar after bar

definitions.text: Slow movement is this, bar after bar

blocks.note: surface reading: a slow passage in music, played bar after bar
setter's reading: a slow, unsteady progress from one pub to the next

explanation.surface: A music teacher describes a slow movement played out measure by measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' and 'movement' pull towards music; the bars are drinking places and the movement is a tour of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour of several drinking establishments in one evening, taken at a leisurely or wobbly pace, is what this phrase names.

clue.text: What has branches providing part of our capital

blocks.note: first meaning: a tall tree
second meaning: a district of East London

explanation.surface: A bank with branches seems to fund a piece of the national capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' and 'capital' suggest a bank and its money; one is a tree, the other a London district, Poplar in the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a common tall tree and the name of a district in London's Tower Hamlets borough.

clue.text: Like wreck exposed, full of salt

indicators.note: something full of a substance holds it within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: exposed means laid bare
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt, sodium chloride

explanation.surface: A shipwreck lies exposed on the shore, encrusted with sea salt.
explanation.walkthrough: Salt here is chemistry: sodium chloride, written NaCl.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreck long under the sea becomes encrusted with these small shellfish that cling to submerged surfaces.

clue.text: Show more flexibility to interpret a part

blocks.note: to read a situation is to interpret it
taken as written
PT is the usual abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: An actor must be more flexible to interpret a role.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust again to new conditions is to show further flexibility, bending to suit circumstances once more.

clue.text: Please repeat your statement about European crop

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: the blunt word said when asking someone to say it again
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone asks a speaker to repeat a remark about European agriculture.
explanation.definitionFit: This cereal grass is one of the most widely grown food crops, milled into flour.

clue.text: Work of art that's drawn by English lake

blocks.note: to go by a place is to go past it
E is the abbreviation for English
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A painting attracts visitors beside a lake in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn by' reads as 'attracted by'; 'drawn' belongs to the definition and 'by' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made with chalky coloured crayon sticks is drawn rather than painted.

clue.text: In contact with, not friends with

blocks.note: first meaning: touching or leaning on, as a ladder on a wall
second meaning: opposed to

explanation.surface: Someone is in touch with a person yet not on good terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means both touching something physically and being in opposition or hostile to someone.

clue.text: What's clearly smelt with head cut off, or another fish

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a strong bad odour is something plainly smelt

explanation.surface: A smelly fish is beheaded, or perhaps a different species is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Smelt is a fish too, which is why the definition says 'another fish'.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater member of the carp family is a fish distinct from the smelt the surface mentions.

clue.text: Volume with American spelling at one reading class

blocks.note: the US spelling of litre, a unit of volume
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A book in American spelling is used at a reading lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book; here it is a unit of capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-read, literary elite form a class of people known for their reading.

clue.text: Unusual play, Act I being modified

indicators.note: something modified has been changed, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A theatre production is unusual because its first act has been changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not typical of its kind is out of the ordinary, which is a synonym.

clue.text: For each artist successively putting final pieces of painting inside steel drawer

indicators.note: the closing pieces of a word are its last letters
the selected letters are placed within something else

blocks.note: per means for each
the French painter Manet, taken twice in a row
the last two letters of the word

explanation.surface: Each artist in turn adds the final touches of a painting inside a steel drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two closing letters go one into each Manet: N into the first, G into the second, each before the final E-T. A drawer here is something that draws, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer is anything that pulls, and this lasting magnet attracts steel to itself.

clue.text: A reason for current stoppage by paragon of industry in firm

blocks.note: taken as written
a barrier that halts the flow of a river current
the ant is the proverbial model of hard work

explanation.surface: A power cut is blamed on an exemplary industrialist inside a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as electricity and 'firm' as a company; the current is a river's and firm is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshakeable in their opinion is resolute, which is a sense of the adjective firm.

clue.text: Face then run after the big cat

indicators.note: placed after means coming next in order behind the word before

blocks.note: pan is slang for the face
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone must face up to a large wild cat, then run from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The run goes after 'the', so the article belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This large wild feline, usually a black leopard, is one of the big cats.

clue.text: Following old philosophy, sorted out optical illusion finally

indicators.note: things sorted out are put into a new arrangement
finally points to the closing letter of the word

blocks.note: the letters of this word
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An optical illusion is finally cleared up by applying ancient philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the seven letters gives P-L-A-T-O-I-C, with the final letter slotted in after PLATO.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things in line with the teachings of the ancient Greek thinker Plato.

clue.text: Stage in preparation of shot, say, in local

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a local is a native of the place
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A step in getting a gunshot ready takes place in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'local' suggest a drink in the pub; the shot is a photograph and a local is a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: In film photography the reversed-tone image is the intermediate stage from which prints of a shot are made.

clue.text: Understood sensitivity surrounding self-referential letter

indicators.note: surrounding means going around another piece

blocks.note: tact is sensitivity in dealing with others
the letter a speaker uses to refer to themselves

explanation.surface: A letter about oneself is quietly understood thanks to sensitivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied without being stated is understood silently, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: What makes us buy too much cutlery? I'd ordered in error

definitions.text: What makes us buy too much

indicators.note: something ordered by mistake is put in the wrong arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders why so much cutlery arrived and blames an ordering mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: To buy a story is to believe it, so buying too much is believing too easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too ready to believe things is gullibility; buy means accept as true in idiom.

clue.text: Turned up book I study for characters showing feeling

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
taken as written
to con is to study or learn

explanation.surface: Someone finds a book and studies its characters for signs of emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' reads as people in a novel; they are typed symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley face built from keyboard symbols conveys a mood in a message.

clue.text: Way to address lady in Mothers' Union?

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a dam is an animal's mother, joined to the first mother

explanation.surface: Members of a women's church organisation wonder how to address a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mothers' Union is a Christian charity; here it is read as a joining of two words for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the polite form of address for a woman, as in 'Dear Sir or ...'.

clue.text: Is daughter cutting food making mistake with hands?

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter
a meal is food

explanation.surface: A daughter slicing food clumsily makes a mistake with her hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The hands are hands of cards, not the body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Distributing playing cards wrongly is an error made with the hands dealt out at the table.

clue.text: Haul back organ for traveller in strange places

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to lug is to haul
the liver is a body organ

explanation.surface: A traveller hauls a church organ back from strange lands.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift's hero voyages to Lilliput, Brobdingnag and other odd lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift's fictional voyager visits bizarre lands of tiny and giant people.

clue.text: Profane brat promises to achieve redemption

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
IOUs are written promises to pay, redeemed when settled

explanation.surface: A wicked child promises to seek redemption.
explanation.walkthrough: Redemption sounds religious, matching Profane; here it is paying off a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking reverence for God or sacred things is the meaning shared by both adjectives.

clue.text: One leader who may be responsible for another

definitions.text: One leader who may be responsible for another

blocks.note: surface reading: a chief or head of some group
setter's reading: a newspaper boss, who oversees the leading article

explanation.walkthrough: A leader is a newspaper's main opinion piece, so the person in charge of a paper is a leader responsible for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a newspaper directs its staff and typically writes or approves the main opinion column.

clue.text: Class schedule ready to print

blocks.note: a type is a class or kind
to set a date is to schedule it

explanation.surface: A school timetable is ready to go to the printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Text laid out in type is composed and ready for printing.

clue.text: Letters from old man for adorable Chinese native

blocks.note: old man is PA, a father; its two letters joined by a conjunction

explanation.surface: Letters from an elderly man are about a cute animal from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters from' means the separate letters of PA, read as P and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bear found wild only in China is famously endearing.

clue.text: Interpret former poet

blocks.note: ex means former
Ezra Pound, the American poet

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to make sense of a poet from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out the meaning of something in detail is to explain it, which is a sense of interpret.

clue.text: Person with insignificant role taken out of context? Rarely

indicators.note: taken out of means lifted from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An actor with a bit part is seldom quoted out of context.
explanation.definitionFit: A film walk-on who appears in crowd scenes without lines has the least significant role.

clue.text: Investor's action perturbed eco-warrior

indicators.note: something perturbed is disturbed and thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: An environmental campaigner is upset by what an investor has done.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner for protecting nature and the environment is a green activist.

clue.text: Almost new and ahead of its time

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
ahead of time means early

explanation.surface: Something is almost new and advanced for its era.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means very close to but not quite, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: From whom one can get nary a yes?

definitions.text: From whom one can get nary a yes?

indicators.note: what one can get from words by working on them is a rearranged version

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone asks who never says yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a person who always refuses, while the last three words supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual refuser or pessimist never agrees, so not a single assent can be got from them.
